contract.words: Get me $2,500 of settled cash within 21 days, selling only to independent cideries. I have no money to put in up front.

terms.proofCondition: first cidery payment settled in the owner's account

strategy.title: Sell three $1,500 cidery website rebuilds, paid in full up front, built by a subcontracted freelance WordPress designer paid only from settled client money
strategy.why: Independent cideries are a published, reachable population (Wikipedia's state-by-state list of ~850 US cideries, each with its own site; ACA says a third of US cideries are members). A 5-page site at $1,500 sits at the bottom of published freelancer prices for small-business sites ($1,500-$7,000, WPZOOM 2026-09-28) and well below a winery agency's $5,000 entry package. A freelancer can build it for ~$500 (dev.to 2026 range $500-$5,000), so three paid-in-full orders settle $4,500 and leave $2,869 after the $1,500 subcontract and Stripe fees, with zero owner money at risk because the designer is paid only after the client's payment settles. What no source establishes is whether cideries buy this from a cold email at this price (demand, price acceptance, conversion), and the designer's written quote; the first-week test measures exactly those before any cost is committed.

alternatives.title: Cider label design subcontracted to a freelance designer ($1,000 per SKU)
alternatives.why: Only one agency list price ($1,000 per beer label, 6-week delivery) supports the price, designer cost is unknown, and the 6-week delivery plus a deposit-only model makes $2,500 settled in 21 days with zero owner capital unlikely; kept as the fallback offer to cideries that decline a website.

alternatives.title: Monthly social media content management for cideries ($399/month)
alternatives.why: Needs seven paying cideries in 21 days, the only price evidence is one non-cider freelancer's limited-time rate, and the subcontractor cost is unknown; dominated by the website route.

reviews.reasons: The shape is sound: CONDITIONAL on demand, price acceptance and conversion; no offer goes out until a written designer quote of <= $500 exists (s1 gate), the designer is paid only from settled client money, and exposure is $0. Recomputed: 3 x $1,500 = $4,500; Stripe 3 x ($43.50 + $0.30) = $131.40; designer 3 x $500 = $1,500; net $2,868.60 (2 sales net only $1,912.40, so 3 are needed); threshold 3 paid of 450 carries the target. Settlement: first live payment day 7, first payout 7-14 days later = day 14-21, so the ledger's day 20 is inside the window only at the short end and lands on day 21 at the long end - no slack. The decisive problem is market volume: the plan needs 450 independent cideries with dated or missing websites and a reachable email, and its only basis is the Wikipedia list it describes as '~850 US cideries, each with its own site'. I verified that list for this goal's buyerVolume question: entries are city wiki links or plain text (about 1% link to an external site), the list includes breweries, vineyards, entries marked CLOSED and corporate-owned brands, and independence is not marked; that research was blocked. Filtering ~850 listed producers to independent cideries, then to those with dated or missing sites, then to those with a findable email, is unlikely to leave 450, and at fewer contacts the 3-of-450 rate no longer reaches the target. The ACA quote ('about a third ... are in our membership') gives no count either.

Only independent cideries may be sold to, and no source counts them: the Wikipedia list (~854 entries) mixes breweries, vineyards, closed and corporate-owned producers and links a site for ~1% of entries (I verified this), and the ACA quote gives only a share. The website route needs 3 paid orders (net $2,868.60 after $131.40 Stripe fees and $1,500 designer cost; 2 orders net only $1,912.40), so the size of the reachable pool decides whether any cold-email test can carry $2,500 in 21 days. That count is a research question Brain can answer at $0 with reads (CHEAP_MODEL_READS present), so it precedes the conversion test rather than being guessed into it. The decision rule (>=450 -> 3-of-450 test; 150-449 -> resized test; <150 -> stop) is coherent, spends nothing and takes no orders. The false 'each with its own site' claim is removed.
findings: Decisive gap correctly named: count of operating, independently owned cideries with a findable email and a dated or missing site.
Arithmetic carried forward correctly: 3 sales, $4,500 gross, $2,868.60 net.
Time budget: the count takes days 1-3 of 21; the follow-on plan must close its first order by about day 7 to clear Stripe's 7-14 day first-payout wait, as the answer notes.
When the CONDITIONAL plan is resubmitted it must restore a fulfilment gate (a written designer quote <= $500) with an executor that can obtain it (messaging is NOT_CONNECTED).

strategy.title: No plan yet: first count the independent cideries a website offer can actually reach
strategy.why: The best route (a $1,500 subcontracted cidery website, paid in full, zero owner money at risk) only carries $2,500 if 3 cideries pay, which at any plausible cold-email rate needs several hundred independent cideries with dated or missing sites and a findable email. No source counts them: the Wikipedia list (~854 entries) mixes breweries, vineyards, closed and corporate-owned producers and carries a website for ~1% of entries, and the ACA gives only a share (a third are members), not a number. Until that count exists there is no plan to judge, and a cold-email test sized on a guessed pool would be uninterpretable.

answers.finding: Arithmetic checks: $4,500 gross, $131.40 fees, $1,500 designer, $2,868.60 net; 3 sales are required.
answers.resolution: Accepted: the arithmetic ($4,500 gross, $131.40 fees, $1,500 designer, $2,868.60 net, 3 sales required) is kept as the target the count must support.

answers.finding: Settlement has no slack: payout of the day-7 payment lands day 14-21 under Stripe's first-payout wait; a day-10 payment settles in time only if subsequent payouts are on the 2-business-day schedule.
answers.resolution: Accepted: settlement has no slack under Stripe's 7-14 day first payout; the resized plan will close the first order by day 7 at the latest or not proceed.
